newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesian central bank intervenes in market.
newsitem.headline: Indonesian central bank intervenes in market.

text.p: Indonesian central bank intervened in the foreign exchange market on Monday following speculative offshore attacks on the rupiah, dealers said.
They said the central bank was seen selling dollar forward outright, which pushed the rupiah higher and swaps lower.
"The intervention seemed to help calm the market. But the overall appetite for dollars remains strong. There are still attempts to test the (intervention) band," one dealer said.
Dealers said the central bank intervention pushed the rupiah up to 2,590 before easing back to 2,610/20 at 0700 GMT.
Confirmation from the central bank was not immediately available.
They said the central bank was seen selling six-, three- and one-month dollars outright at the 2,745, 2,685 and 2,638 levels respectively.
One European bank dealer said swaps fell after the intervention, but the tone remained biddish.
One-month swaps fell to 30.0 from 60.0 points.
